'''Distant Blade''' (Japanese: {{hl|後背の刃|Kōhai no ha}} ''Blade of the Hinterlands'') is the ninth chapter of [[Eirika]]'s route in {{FE8}}.

==Plot==
{{main|Distant Blade/Script}}
As [[Eirika]] makes her way towards [[Rausten]], Emperor [[Vigarde]] relays new orders to his generals in [[Grado]] Keep. Vigarde sends [[Glen]] to capture Eirika and [[Valter]] to [[Ephraim]]; [[Caellach]] to destroy the [[Sacred Stone (object)|Sacred Stone]] of [[Jehanna]] and [[Riev]] to destroy Rausten's stone; and [[Duessel]] to fight Ephraim and [[Frelia]]. Vigarde tells [[Selena (The Sacred Stones)|Selena]] to await further orders in the capital.

Outside of Port Kiris in [[Carcino]], [[Tana]] catches [[Eirika]] and asks to join her army. Eirika initially refuses, but acquiesces when Tana insists.

Once at Port Kiris, [[Seth]] ensures Eirika remembers the fake identity they agreed she would use to avoid enemies of [[Renais]]. Before they can seek a ship to their destination, Eirika notices [[L'Arachel]] nearby; Eirika approaches and greets her. L'Arachel offers Eirika a pastry, but explains that ships are afraid to set sail for fear of a "giant ghost ship" in the waters. L'Arachel suggests that Eirika instead pass through the longer overland route to reach Rausten, before departing for Rausten with [[Dozla]] and [[Rennac]]. After they leave, Eirika is approached by a mercenary by the name of [[Binks]]; he asks if she is Princess Eirika of Renais, and intends to capture her for a bounty.

During the battle, reinforcements from Grado appear on the battlefield; among their ranks is a fresh recruit named [[Amelia]]. [[Franz]] or Eirika can approach Amelia, and will assume she is a citizen and attempt to get her to safety; Amelia corrects them, but is persuaded to join them when she no longer believes what Grado has said about Eirika's character. Alternately, the Grado soldiers—with Amelia in tow—will leave the battle when the mercenaries are not winning definitively.

Once the mercenaries are routed, Seth corners one of the remaining mercenaries and interrogates him; the mercenary states that [[Pablo]], one of the members of the Carcino Council of Elders, hired him. Eirika realizes that [[Innes]] is in danger as he was going to pass through Carcino to reach Jehanna. Then, a messenger arrives to inform Eirika that Innes has been trapped by Carcino's forces in a siege; Eirika sends the messenger to Frelia and assures them that she will save the prince herself. If the player visited each of the villages, Rennac—one of L'Arachel's attendants—approaches Eirika; he asks if L'Arachel and Dozla have left, and rejoices when Eirika confirms they have.

==Strategy==
{{strategy}}
The first challenge is to push through the enemies at the top of the map. You will want to move quickly, likely with help from mounted units if you intend to save the western Village (which yields a [[Dracoshield]]). The [[Pirate]] who starts closest will take several turns to reach it, so try to break through to him at a brisk pace. On Difficult mode, a Pirate starts at the top of the map, and he'll move a lot faster due to not starting on water tiles, so you'll need to move faster to catch him. Difficult mode also gives the [[Sniper]] massive stat increases compared to normal and easy, so bring someone strong like [[Seth]] to take care of him.

The other Village only contains another [[Rapier]] for [[Eirika]], but saving both will net you an [[Angelic Robe]]. While fliers can reach it in fairly short order, it'll be much safer by taking care of the Pirate below where you start, since there are [[Archer]]s that deal effective damage near the village. Pirate [[Ross]] can bait out the Pirate to have the village be in no immediate danger, so it can be visited at your leisure.

Even if you do not wish to train her, [[Amelia]]'s [[Speedwing]] is a valuable acquisition. If not looking to recruit Amelia at all, [[Colm]] can [[Steal]] it. As a bonus, when Amelia reappears in [[Hamill Canyon|Chapter&nbsp;13]], she'll have another Speedwing that can be stolen, or be traded away after recruiting Amelia there, which can be done at the player's discretion. Regardless of whether you're trying to recruit Amelia or steal here Speedwing, avoid entering her attack range until you are ready to engage her, as she will attack anyone in range and likely fall to the counter. However, since she has only 4 Move, the [[Soldier]]s surrounding her can all be baited to charge at someone outside of her attack range. If aiming to recruit, an Eirika positioned six spaces away once the coast is clear, can talk to Amelia from outside of her range.

[[Binks]] is easy to beat once the [[Mercenary|Mercenaries]] and reinforcements are dealt with. He is immobile, and the [[Axereaver]] dropped by a nearby Soldier puts him at a great disadvantage. Even if no one on your team can tank an attack, Binks does not have a [[Hand Axe]] or any form of healing, so as a last resort you could attack uncounterably, Rescue the attacker away to safety using a mounted unit's [[Canto]], and repeat until he is defeated.
